about: The Disappointed Pakistani Fan is a broadcast shot of a bald cricket supporter in a checked red shirt and navy gilet standing in the stands with his hands on his hips, mouth set, staring ahead with total weary disbelief while the fans around him look just as glum. His posture says he expected little and somehow still got let down. It has become a universal reaction for quiet, exasperated disappointment, the kind that is too tired for anger.
origin: The fan, Muhammad Sarim Akhtar, was caught on camera during the Australia vs Pakistan match at the 2019 Cricket World Cup on June 12, 2019. The frame spread quickly as a reaction image beyond cricket.
usage:
Top box: the situation or expectation. Bottom box: the letdown. The two lines usually read as one sentence, with the deflating detail saved for the end.

It suits small, repeated disappointments rather than tragedies: opening the fridge to the same food, a team blowing a lead again, a sequel trailer, an hour-long call that should have been a two-line message. His stance fits best when the disappointment was predictable.
ideas: and it's still the same food
my team up by 3 goals at halftime
they removed the one feature i used
you finally get the day off
